mfg1-electrical-l057.title: Apply 3R and circular-economy thinking to electrical products
mfg1-electrical-l057.objective: Separate 3R goals from permission to use an item, and preserve safety in resource circulation.

paragraphs.title: Reduce, reuse, and recycle
paragraphs.text: Reduce limits waste generation, reuse uses products again, and recycle recovers resources. Reducing packaging, reusing returnable boxes, and separating materials have different aims. Do not remove packaging needed for protection.

paragraphs.title: Consider circulation from design onward
paragraphs.text: A circular economy facilitates repair and reuse and keeps products and materials in circulation longer. It also considers pollution prevention, renewable energy, and the natural environment. Identify reused items and inspect suitability; do not unconditionally return safety parts to service.

paragraphs.title: Check electrical conditions too
paragraphs.text: DC is basically unidirectional, whereas AC periodically changes direction. DC can vary in magnitude while retaining direction. Do not assume recovered power supplies or batteries are interchangeable from shape or marked voltage alone: check ratings, polarity, and condition.

terms.meaning: The three actions of waste reduction, reuse, and resource recovery.
An economic approach that circulates resources to reduce waste and environmental burden.
Using products or similar items repeatedly.
Distinguishing positive and negative, for example.

mfg1-electrical-l057.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Classify returnable-box reuse, offcut reduction, and copper-wire separation under 3R. Describe checks and storage when handling recovered batteries.
safety: Do not short battery terminals; identify and store recovered items as specified.
mfg1-electrical-l057.summary: Separate 3R goals from permission to use an item, and preserve safety in resource circulation.

mfg1-electrical-l058.title: Check laws, technical requirements, and PSE separately
mfg1-electrical-l058.objective: Separate product, installation, and worker conditions, and verify the applicable date.

paragraphs.title: Purpose and scope
paragraphs.text: The Electrical Appliances and Materials Safety Act aims to prevent hazards from covered electrical products. PSE marks apply to covered items, with different shapes for specified products and other products. Match classification, notifying business, and ratings with product documents; a mark alone does not prove suitability for every use.

paragraphs.title: Different from installation requirements
paragraphs.text: The ministerial ordinance on technical standards for electrical installations concerns installation performance requirements. Its interpretation gives technical details for meeting them. Choosing a product, connecting it to an installation, and verifying workers’ qualifications or training are separate checks.

paragraphs.title: Notice when information applies
paragraphs.text: Do not unconditionally apply textbook item counts or grounding-omission examples to all current products. Confirm required markings, installation conditions, and qualifications using current public guidance and the responsible person. An earth-leakage breaker does not authorize removing grounding.

terms.meaning: Electrical products and materials within a statutory category.
A mark associated with the safety system for covered electrical products.
An order issued by a ministry’s minister.
Technical requirements that installations or similar things must satisfy.

mfg1-electrical-l058.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Separate PSE coverage, installation suitability, and worker authorization into three columns. List checks for an AC adapter with unknown specifications.
safety: Do not guess legal or grounding applicability when installing equipment or omitting protection.
mfg1-electrical-l058.summary: Separate product, installation, and worker conditions, and verify the applicable date.

mfg1-electrical-l059.title: Identify domestic, international, and industry standards
mfg1-electrical-l059.objective: Match issuer, scope, edition, and differences.

paragraphs.title: Issuer and scope
paragraphs.text: JIS are national standards; JEM concerns the electrical manufacturing industry, JEITA electronics and information technology, and JSIA distribution/control systems. Different names have different scopes and issuers. Distinguish basic standards for terms and units, test-method standards, and product standards.

paragraphs.title: International and overseas requirements
paragraphs.text: IEC develops international electrical standards, while ISO covers wider international standardization. NEC, VDE, and IEEE differ in region, organization, and scope. Check the requirements of the destination country and contract for exported products.

paragraphs.title: Do not assume equivalence
paragraphs.text: Even where JIS and IEC have corresponding standards, check editions and differences before treating them as identical. For drawings with old and new symbols, consult the legend and applicable standard. Record number, edition year, and relevant sections before applying them to assembly conditions.

terms.meaning: The organization conducting international electrical standardization.
A standard established by an industry association.
An edition indicating when a standard was issued or revised.
Bringing requirements into correspondence.

mfg1-electrical-l059.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Before using a domestic part in an export panel, organize checks for destination, standard number, edition, differences, and approved drawing.
safety: An overseas standard name alone does not guarantee protective functions or rating suitability.
mfg1-electrical-l059.summary: Match issuer, scope, edition, and differences.

mfg1-electrical-l060.title: Drawing types, paper sizes, and third-angle projection
mfg1-electrical-l060.objective: Align drawing identification and viewing direction to read shape.

paragraphs.title: Which drawing to use
paragraphs.text: Distinguish drawings by purpose such as production, planning, or approval; expression such as outline, exploded view, or connections; and content such as parts, assembly, or layout. A parts list identifies components. Check title block, number, revision, and sheet count, and do not mix another product’s drawing in.

paragraphs.title: Paper and borders
paragraphs.text: A4 is 210×297 mm and A3 is 297×420 mm. Halving a larger A-series sheet gives the next size. Check borders, title block, and margins, and use written dimensions even on resized printouts. Do not confuse paper size with product dimensions.

paragraphs.title: Viewing direction and placement
paragraphs.text: In third-angle projection, the top view is above the front view, the right-side view to the right, and the left-side view to the left. Relate visible and hidden shapes across views and check the projection symbol. Not every country or drawing uses third-angle projection.

terms.meaning: An orthographic projection that places views on the corresponding viewing side.
A field containing drawing number, name, and related information.
A list of components making up an assembly.
The main projected view chosen to represent shape and function.

mfg1-electrical-l060.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Draw a layout explaining front, top, and right views of a small stepped part. Write a clarification request when number, revision, or projection method is unknown.
safety: Do not guess hole positions or cuts from a drawing whose interpretation is unclear.
mfg1-electrical-l060.summary: Align drawing identification and viewing direction to read shape.

mfg1-electrical-l061.title: Dimension, roughness, and fit requirements
mfg1-electrical-l061.objective: Read dimensions, roughness, and fits as different requirements.

paragraphs.title: Lines and dimensions
paragraphs.text: Outlines, hidden lines, centerlines, dimension lines, cutting positions, and hatching have different meanings. Dimensions state finished requirements; distinguish radiusR, diameterφ, arc, chord, and angle. Do not infer lengths or angles from appearance.

paragraphs.title: Roughness and manufacturing method
paragraphs.text: Ra is arithmetic mean roughness: under comparable conditions, a smaller value describes a smoother surface. Do not confuse roughness inμm with dimensions inmm; check machining notes too. Symbols vary by standard and edition, so do not assume old symbols are current.

paragraphs.title: Judge shaft and hole together
paragraphs.text: Clearance, interference, and transition fits depend on the combination of shaft and hole dimensional limits. The same nominal size does not establish the same actual relationship. Do not independently press-fit or heat parts; confirm tolerances and approved assembly methods.

terms.reading: さんじゅつへいきんあらさ
terms.meaning: Ra, an indicator of surface irregularity magnitude.
The combination of permitted shaft and hole dimensions.
A fit that can produce clearance or interference depending on the allowed dimensions.
Parallel sloping lines indicating a section or similar feature.

mfg1-electrical-l061.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Calculate clearance for a 20.02 mm hole and 19.98 mm shaft, and explain why nominal 20 mm alone is insufficient. Distinguish Ra 3.2 μm from 3.2 mm.
safety: Do not force or heat an assembly whose tolerances are unknown.
mfg1-electrical-l061.summary: Read dimensions, roughness, and fits as different requirements.

mfg1-electrical-l062.title: Electrical symbols and the order of reading a ladder
mfg1-electrical-l062.objective: Match terminals, device identity, and state; separate logic from actual wiring.

paragraphs.title: Identify devices through symbols
paragraphs.text: Match resistor, variable resistor, capacitor, coil, diode, LED, transistor, fuse, meter, and contact symbols with names. Light arrows differ between an emitting LED and a receiving photodiode. Also match terminal roles such as A/K and B/C/E.

paragraphs.title: Link separated contacts
paragraphs.text: An expanded connection diagram can place one relay’s coil and contacts apart. Link them through device identifiers and references rather than assuming nearby contacts belong together. Distinguish normal from operated states: a contacts close and b contacts open on operation.

paragraphs.title: A ladder is not a picture of physical wiring
paragraphs.text: Learn basic PLC ladders through evaluating conditions from top to bottom and left to right. Distinguish inputs, internal relays, and outputs, and do not confuse a/b instructions with physical switch wiring. Consult the model specification for actual evaluation order and special instructions.

terms.meaning: A connection diagram expanded to make operating relationships easier to read.
A diagram or program expressing control conditions in ladder form.
An element retaining a condition state inside a controller.
Information locating a related symbol.

mfg1-electrical-l062.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Describe conditions involving input P, internal relay M, and lamp Y. Explain how to find contacts sharing a coil identifier, and distinguish an LED from a light-receiving device.
safety: Do not independently change safety circuits on the basis of learning symbols.
mfg1-electrical-l062.summary: Match terminals, device identity, and state; separate logic from actual wiring.

mfg1-electrical-l063.title: Conductive and magnetic materials and thermal classes
mfg1-electrical-l063.objective: Check electrical, magnetic, and thermal properties separately.

paragraphs.title: Differences between wire materials
paragraphs.text: Annealed copper has reduced work hardening and differs from hard copper and aluminum in strength, conductivity, mass, and other properties. Material changes resistance even at equal length and cross-section. Not attracting a magnet does not mean not conducting electricity.

paragraphs.title: Retaining or changing magnetism
paragraphs.text: Electrical steel uses measures such as thin laminated sheets to reduce losses from changing flux. Select permanent-magnet materials by remanence, coercivity, and use. Do not substitute every magnetic material as the same core or permanent magnet.

paragraphs.title: Insulation temperature conditions
paragraphs.text: The textbook’s thermal-class examples are Y90, A105, E120, B130, F155, H180, and R220°C. These concern materials or insulation systems under specified conditions, not every product’s ambient temperature. Natural rubber is not inorganic insulation: use mica and ceramics as examples. Do not misclassify paper-based materials as inorganic either.

terms.meaning: A controlled heating treatment that softens a material.
A property related to the magnetic field needed to cancel retained magnetization.
Steel sheet designed to reduce losses in cores and similar applications.
A thermal classification of insulation under defined conditions.

mfg1-electrical-l063.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Make tables comparing equal-sized copper and aluminum, cores and permanent magnets, and thermal classes versus ambient temperature.
safety: Do not decide operating temperature or replacement suitability from thermal class alone.
mfg1-electrical-l063.summary: Check electrical, magnetic, and thermal properties separately.
